_comment: Enemy roster. SIX types in version one: Sweepers, Stockers, Glimmers, WindowWalkers, Ficus, Warden. Every enemy must telegraph with sound before sight - that is an accessibility requirement, not polish.
_retuneNote: Chris's call, 2026-11-04: EVERY moveSpeed in this file halved as part of the movement retune, because the player's walk/sprint/crouch halved and a chase is a ratio. Stockers 8>4, Glimmers 18>9, WindowWalkers 8>4, Ficus 6>3, Warden 16>8. Sweepers went 14>6 rather than 14>7 - the one deliberate ratio change, for the escape invariant, and its own note below has the arithmetic. Every other enemy's speed as a fraction of sprint is IDENTICAL to what it was before the retune: Glimmers 0.783, Warden 0.696, Stockers and WindowWalkers 0.348, Ficus 0.261. This is why the whole file moved and not just the Sweeper: halving the player alone left Glimmers at 504 cm/s and the Warden at 448 against a 322 cm/s sprint, so two enemies became literally inescapable. Chris warned about exactly that failure - 'we should not lower player speed alone and accidentally make the Sweeper impossible' - and the balance suite caught it on the enemy he did not name. tests/movement.test.mjs now asserts no enemy outruns a clean sprint, so the next rescale cannot repeat it.
_scopeNote: History of this line, because it has moved twice and both moves were approvals rather than drift. It read 'four types' until the edit that added WindowWalkers deleted it; Chris approved that fifth type on 2026-10-20. Codex added the ficus concept art and Chris approved it the same day ('Codex did it, I like the ficus'), making six. A seventh needs his approval the same way. The rule is not the number - it is that a guardrail moves deliberately and never gets removed by whoever needs it out of the way.
_ficusTodo: APPROVED and NOW DEFINED - this note said otherwise until 2026-10-28, by which time it was wrong. The Ficus row exists below with a full stat line, and ELLKEnemyFamily carries the value. Concept art is at assets/enemies/ficus-stalker-concept-v1.png. A mall local per docs/ZONES.md, like the WindowWalkers - derived from mall landscaping. What is still outstanding is only the art and the in-engine actor; the data is done. Its stats remain Chris's call, as all values in this file are.

Sweepers.behaviour: Weak alone. Swarm lit players and dropped loot.
Sweepers.counterplay: Kill lights, move, or drop loot as a decoy.
Sweepers._moveSpeedNote: Chris's call, 2026-11-04, as part of the movement retune. Was 14. Halving the player's speeds would have put this at 7, which PRESERVES the ratio that was already broken - so it takes one further stud off. The invariant is that sprint must always escape a stumbled Sweeper, and it has to hold in the worst legal state, which is stumbled AND carrying three relics: the stumble multiplier and the burden multiplier compound at LLKCharacter.cpp:572. At 7 studs the worst state clears by 2.4 cm/s, which is nothing. At 6 it clears by 21.7. In fractions of sprint this moves the Sweeper from 0.609 to 0.522, against a ceiling of stumbleMultiplier x minBurdenMultiplier = 0.616. 168 cm/s is 1.68 m/s, faster than a human walk and slower than this game's - a machine that never hurries and never stops. docs/PROPOSAL-MOVEMENT-RETUNE.md has the full table.

Stockers.behaviour: Slow, tall, strong line of sight.
Stockers.counterplay: Break sight and pass in darkness.

Glimmers.behaviour: Complete a 2-second scan, then tag one player for 20 seconds.
Glimmers.counterplay: Go dark before the scan completes; break sight and relocate if tagged.

WindowWalkers.behaviour: Remain still until a nearby active lantern catches them, then walk directly after the light source.
WindowWalkers.counterplay: Go dark and break sight; they do not navigate around a lost target.

Ficus.behaviour: Stands as a potted plant until lantern light catches it, then creeps after the light source.
Ficus.counterplay: Go dark, break sight, and do not light every decorative plant in a department store.

Warden.behaviour: Converges on the brightest position once the Warden's own arrival meter fills - see zone-pressure.json `warden`, which Chris split out of the generic thresholds on 2026-10-28. It is a late-night escalation, not the normal consequence of using a lantern. Brightest position, never nearest player: that is what puts cause and consequence in the same pair of hands.
Warden.counterplay: Hide, kite, distract, or extract. Never kill it.
Warden._comment: Not a boss. It is the mall zone's final warning given a body. If it ever becomes killable, the pressure clock stops meaning anything.
